biography: Pedro Pimenta, a name whispered with respect in the Brazilian Opala Old Stock Race scene, hails from the dusty karting tracks of Ribeirão Preto. Unlike many racers with silver-spoon beginnings, Pedro's journey began with a battered kart salvaged from a junkyard by his mechanic father. He honed his skills on makeshift circuits, a raw talent nurtured by relentless practice and a keen understanding of vehicle mechanics. His breakthrough came at the 2018 Ribeirão Preto Karting Championship, where he clinched victory after a daring last-lap overtake that saw him brush the barriers – a move that cemented his reputation as a calculating risk-taker. Transitioning to the Opala Old Stock Race in 2020, Pedro quickly adapted to the heavy, powerful machines. He currently drives for a small, privately funded team, consistently punching above their weight, proving that raw talent and strategic brilliance can overcome financial limitations. His meticulous approach to race preparation and his uncanny ability to extract every ounce of performance from his Opala have made him a force to be reckoned with.
drivingStyle: Pedro's driving style is best described as 'controlled aggression.' He meticulously studies track data and opponent behavior, identifying vulnerabilities and exploiting them with surgical precision. While capable of breathtaking overtakes, he prioritizes consistency and tire management. He is known for his late-braking maneuvers and his ability to maintain momentum through corners, sacrificing a bit of entry speed for a faster exit. Under pressure, Pedro remains remarkably calm, making calculated decisions based on real-time data and track conditions. He doesn't often make mistakes, preferring to bide his time and strike when the opportunity is optimal.

careerHighlight: Winning the 2022 Interlagos Old Stock Race after starting from 12th on the grid. He executed a brilliant tire management strategy and capitalized on late-race chaos to snatch victory in the final lap.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the 2021 Curitiba Old Stock Race due to a mechanical failure while leading the race. The incident cost him valuable championship points and left him questioning his team's reliability.
